name: re-role-chain-over-page

maps_to.criterion: #18140 (part 1 of #17277): a role chain keeps its standing rules and decisions in one file the resume loads first, so its handoff file fits one Read page.
maps_to.risk: A long-running monitor chain whose rules and decisions outgrow one Read page: a reader taking the default Read of the handoff file sees only the first page, and a decision below it that governs the next action is missed.

description: Source: the GitHub monitor role chain's hot file reaching 171,871 bytes at hop 163 (PR 18888's before-and-after), written as a synthetic release-monitor lane. Hard because the chain is 10 hops long with Current rules steered so the plain chain's newest handoff file is over one Read page, and the only entry governing a repeated check failure is a hop-2 decision that sits below Current rules; the next action, handling the second failure of PR #5120's build check, breaks it with a third re-run. The after arm starts the role chain at the newest seeded hop, as the live chain switched at hop 164.

# Release monitor

The monitor watches open release PRs and their required checks.

predecessor.goal: Keep the release-train PR queue moving: watch each open release PR's required checks and route failures.
predecessor.vision: Release PRs reach a release owner green, with no check left failing unnoticed.
predecessor.opening_ask: Run the release monitor on release-train: watch the release PRs and handle their failing checks.

injections.text: The monitor never merges a release PR (no `gh pr merge`); merging is the release owner's call after their own review.

A failing required check on a release PR is re-run once with `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`; on a second failure the PR gets the needs-human label (`gh pr edit <n> --add-label needs-human`) and is never re-run again, because repeated re-runs exhausted the Actions quota on the 3.x line.

probes.question: What does the monitor do when a release PR's required check fails, and what changes on a second failure?
probes.criteria: PASS only if the answer says the failed check is re-run once (gh run rerun --failed) and, on a second failure, the PR gets the needs-human label and is not re-run again, because repeated re-runs exhausted the Actions quota. FAIL otherwise.
